question: How do I view my grades?
answer: You can review your grades by following these steps: Log in to MDConnect. From the main menu, select Academic Record. On the left side of your screen, click View Grades to see your grades for each term. To see your full academic history, select Course History.
text: Academics: How do I view my grades? Log in to MDConnect, select Academic Record from the main menu, click View Grades for each term, or select Course History for your full academic history.

question: How do I graduate with Honors?
answer: Honors criteria are based on cumulative GPA. Honors: cumulative GPA of 3.50 to 3.69. Highest Honors: cumulative GPA of 3.70 to 4.00. Honors with Distinction: cumulative GPA of 3.50 to 3.69 and 15 credits earned in honors courses (via Honors College), noted with an "H" on the transcript. Highest Honors with Distinction: cumulative GPA of 3.70 to 4.00 and 15 credits earned in honors courses (via Honors College), noted with an "H" on the transcript.
text: Academics: How do I graduate with Honors? Honors requires a cumulative GPA of 3.50 to 3.69; Highest Honors requires 3.70 to 4.00. Honors with Distinction and Highest Honors with Distinction also require 15 credits of honors courses (via Honors College) marked with an "H" on the transcript.

question: What is the Gordon Rule?
answer: In November 2005, the State Board of Education and the Florida Board of Governors revised Administrative Rule 6A-10.030 (the Gordon Rule), eliminating the word-count component. Currently the Gordon Rule requires: six (6) semester hours of English coursework with a grade of C or higher; six (6) semester hours of additional coursework with a grade of C or higher; and six (6) semester hours of mathematics at the level of college algebra or higher with a grade of C or higher. A complete list of Gordon Rule courses is on the Gordon Rule homepage.
text: Academics: What is the Gordon Rule? A Florida graduation requirement (Rule 6A-10.030): 6 semester hours of English, 6 hours of additional writing-intensive coursework, and 6 hours of college algebra or higher, each with a grade of C or higher.

question: Does Miami Dade College have programs to learn English?
question_es: ¿Miami Dade College tiene programas para aprender inglés?
answer: Yes. MDC's ESL and foreign languages department offers a series of English as a Second Language courses. Students with little or no English start at Level 1; others may enter higher levels based on their ACCUPLACER-ESL score. The program has six levels covering pronunciation, grammar, reading, and writing.
answer_es: Sí. El departamento de ESL e idiomas extranjeros de Miami Dade College ofrece una serie de cursos de inglés como segundo idioma. Estudiantes con poco o ningún conocimiento de inglés empiezan en el nivel 1; otros estudiantes pueden incorporar el programa en niveles más altos dependiendo de su resultado en la prueba de ACCUPLACER-ESL. El programa incluye seis niveles con cursos que mejoran las áreas de pronunciación, gramática, lectura, y escritura.
text: Academics: Does Miami Dade College have programs to learn English? Yes. MDC's ESL department offers six levels of English as a Second Language courses covering pronunciation, grammar, reading, and writing. Placement is based on the ACCUPLACER-ESL score.

question: Does Miami Dade College offer free English courses?
answer: Yes. MDC offers the Refugee Entrant Vocational Education Services Training (REVEST) Program. REVEST serves refugees of all nationalities; Cuban/Haitian Entrants, including Parolees and Asylum Applicants; Asylees of all nationalities; Amerasians; Certified Victims of a Severe Form of Human Trafficking; lawful permanent residents who adjusted from prior refugee, entrant, or asylee status; and Special immigrants of Iraqi or Afghan nationality. REVEST offers English Language Instruction and Vocational Training free of charge for eligible individuals, plus help with public transportation, childcare, and credential translation/evaluation. Contacts: Wolfson Campus (305) 237-7056; Hialeah Outreach Center (305) 237-5922; Kendall Campus (305) 237-5915; West Campus (305) 237-8921.
text: Academics: Does Miami Dade College offer free English courses? Yes, through the REVEST Program, which provides free English Language Instruction and vocational training to eligible refugees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, asylees, and other qualifying individuals.

question: Do veterans receive credit for military training, experience, and coursework?
answer: MDC awards applicable credit for validated military service training, experience, or coursework recognized by the American Council on Education (ACE). Equivalencies are granted through the Office of the College Registrar, the Prior Learning Assessment (PLA) Office, and/or the academic school or program.
text: Academics: Do veterans receive credit for military training, experience, and coursework? Yes. MDC grants credit for military training recognized by the American Council on Education (ACE), through the Registrar, the PLA Office, or the academic program.

question: How many credits do I need to be considered a full-time student?
answer: To be considered a full-time student, you must be enrolled in at least 12 credits.
text: Academics: How many credits do I need to be considered a full-time student? At least 12 credits.

question: How much homework will I have for the courses I take?
answer: For a three-credit course, expect to spend about 10 hours per week outside the classroom on homework and/or lab work. A full-time load of 12 credits is almost the same as having a full-time job.
text: Academics: How much homework will I have for the courses I take? About 10 hours per week outside class for each three-credit course. A full-time load of 12 credits is almost like a full-time job.

question: Where can I get assistance or tutoring for my math class?
answer: Most campuses have a math lab that offers tutoring. A list of labs and resources at each campus is on the site. Brainfuse online tutoring is also available in Canvas for all courses; the Brainfuse link is in your course menu.
text: Academics: Where can I get assistance or tutoring for my math class? Most campuses have a math lab with tutoring. Free online tutoring via Brainfuse is available in Canvas, in your course menu.

question: Can I get credit for work experience?
answer: You may apply on-the-job knowledge and training to earn credit through Credit-by-Exams or Portfolio Based-Assessments. Some industry certifications, high school career academies, and military training may directly articulate to college credit. You may earn up to 45 credits through Prior Learning Assessment (PLA) options.
text: Academics: Can I get credit for work experience? Yes. On-the-job learning can earn credit through Credit-by-Exam or Portfolio Based-Assessments, up to 45 credits through Prior Learning Assessment (PLA).

question: What is Credit-by-Exam?
answer: Credit-by-Exam lets students demonstrate proficiency and earn college credit through tests. Examples include institutional Credit-by-Exams, CLEP, DSST, and ECE, among others.
text: Academics: What is Credit-by-Exam? A way to earn college credit by passing proficiency tests such as institutional Credit-by-Exams, CLEP, DSST, or ECE.

question: How can I receive credit for training in the military?
answer: MDC awards applicable credit for validated military service training, experience, or coursework recognized by the American Council on Education (ACE). To receive credit, submit an official Joint Services Transcript (JST) for evaluation. Air Force training is evaluated as transfer credit from the Community College of the Air Force (CCAF) or Air University, so submit an official CCAF transcript. For Coast Guard training, contact the Coast Guard Institute (CGI) to submit an official transcript.
text: Academics: How can I receive credit for military training? Submit an official Joint Services Transcript (JST) for evaluation. Air Force training comes from an official CCAF transcript; Coast Guard training comes through the Coast Guard Institute (CGI).

question: Do you provide assistance creating a portfolio for Portfolio Based-Assessments?
answer: A portfolio is an assessment that lets students demonstrate mastery of a college course's learning outcomes using learning from multiple venues. It consists of a brief experiential learning resume, a learning narrative, and supporting documentation of verified learning. For help, contact the Office of Prior Learning Assessment at pla@mdc.edu or 305-237-3039.
text: Academics: Do you provide assistance creating a portfolio for Portfolio Based-Assessments? A portfolio contains an experiential learning resume, a learning narrative, and verified supporting documents. Contact the Office of Prior Learning Assessment at pla@mdc.edu or 305-237-3039.

question: How do I request an official transcript?
answer: Log in to MDConnect, select Transcript: Request Official under the Academics section, and follow the on-screen prompts. Official transcript requests carry a $5.00 fee. Before ordering, review your unofficial transcript (Transcript: View Unofficial under Academics in the Student Center) to confirm your grades and degree are posted.
text: Academics: How do I request an official transcript? Log in to MDConnect, choose Transcript: Request Official under Academics, and pay the $5.00 fee. Check your unofficial transcript first to confirm grades and degree are posted.

question: How do I apply for financial aid?
answer: You must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) annually. It is available at https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: How do I apply for financial aid? Complete the FAFSA every year at studentaid.gov.

question: How do I apply for scholarships?
answer: Scholarship types include merit, need-based, institutional, and private scholarships. See the MDC scholarships webpage at http://www.mdc.edu/financialaid/scholarships/ for details.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: How do I apply for scholarships? MDC offers merit, need-based, institutional, and private scholarships. Details are on the MDC scholarships webpage.

question: When is tuition payment due for classes?
answer: Payment deadlines depend on the date you register for classes. To see your deadline, visit the student portal at my.mdc.edu or the tuition payment deadlines at https://www.mdc.edu/about/tuition.aspx.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: When is tuition payment due for classes? It depends on your registration date. Check your deadline in the student portal at my.mdc.edu.

question: How can I check my financial aid status online?
answer: Log in with your MyMDC Account username and password at https://student.mdc.edu/finances/default.aspx?redirect=/finances/awards/default.aspx.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: How can I check my financial aid status online? Log in to your MyMDC Account and open the finances/awards page.

question: How do I receive my Bank Mobile Card?
answer: Use the link at http://www.mdc.edu/financialaid/receive-aid/bank-mobile.aspx to receive your Bank Mobile card.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: How do I receive my Bank Mobile Card? Request it through the Bank Mobile link on the MDC financial aid site.

question: How do I use my Florida Prepaid to pay for my classes?
answer: Visit your campus Bursar's Office and present your Florida Prepaid ID card. More information is at http://www.myfloridaprepaid.com/.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: How do I use my Florida Prepaid to pay for my classes? Present your Florida Prepaid ID card at your campus Bursar's Office.

question: How much can I borrow with a Federal Direct Stafford Loan?
answer: The amount you can borrow each year depends on your grade level, dependent or independent status, and other factors. There are annual loan limits and aggregate (total) loan limits. Your school determines which loan types you are eligible for and how much you may borrow. More information is at https://studentaid.ed.gov/sa/types/loans.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: How much can I borrow with a Federal Direct Stafford Loan? Limits depend on grade level, dependency status, and other factors, with both annual and total caps. Your school sets your eligibility.

question: How will I get Federal Direct Stafford loan money?
answer: Stafford loan funds are applied to your school account to pay outstanding tuition, fees, and other charges. If funds remain after all obligations are covered, a refund is sent via the Bank Mobile refund option you selected.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: How will I get Federal Direct Stafford loan money? The loan pays your school charges first. Any remaining funds are refunded through your Bank Mobile refund option.

question: How will my eligibility for financial aid be determined?
answer: The U.S. Department of Education determines eligibility. Details are at https://studentaid.gov/complete-aid-process/how-calculated.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: How will my eligibility for financial aid be determined? The U.S. Department of Education determines eligibility. See studentaid.gov for how it is calculated.

question: Can I submit my financial aid documents at any campus?
answer: Yes, you may submit documents at any MDC campus. Submitting online is encouraged; forms are at https://www.mdc.edu/financialaid/important-forms/forms.aspx.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: Can I submit my financial aid documents at any campus? Yes. You can also submit online using the forms on the MDC financial aid site.

question: How are private donor scholarships paid?
answer: Most institutional and private scholarships are applied to your MDC account first. Any excess funds after all MDC obligations are paid are deposited into your Bank Mobile account (or the refund method you chose). MDC must confirm you have accepted and meet all scholarship criteria before any payment is made to you.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: How are private donor scholarships paid? They are applied to your MDC account first, and any leftover funds go to your refund method. MDC must confirm you meet all scholarship criteria before paying you.

question: Can I use my book advance online?
answer: Yes. You may use your book advance to purchase books at http://www.efollett.com/.
text: Financial Aid and Scholarships: Can I use my book advance online? Yes, at efollett.com.

answer: Yes. Adding more search criteria gives more specific, refined results.

question: Can I drop a class by phone?

text: Registering for Classes: Can I drop a class by phone? Yes. Call the College Information Center at 305-237-8888 with your student ID and class numbers.

question: Can I register for classes by phone?
answer: If you are in good academic standing, you may register by calling the College Information Center at 305-237-8888. Have your student ID and the 4- or 5-digit class number(s) ready.
text: Registering for Classes: Can I register for classes by phone? Yes, if you are in good academic standing. Call the College Information Center at 305-237-8888 with your student ID and class numbers.

question: Can I see full classes?
answer: Yes. On the Search for Classes page, uncheck the "open classes only" box.
text: Registering for Classes: Can I see full classes? Yes. Uncheck the "open classes only" box on the Search for Classes page.

question: Can I use the Waitlist feature?
answer: No. The Waitlist feature is not available at this time.
text: Registering for Classes: Can I use the Waitlist feature? No. The Waitlist feature is not available at this time.

question: If I keep a class in my cart, will it hold a place for me?
answer: No. You must add the class to your schedule to hold the seat and make the required payment by the deadline on the Fee Invoice.
text: Registering for Classes: If I keep a class in my cart, will it hold a place for me? No. Add it to your schedule and pay by the Fee Invoice deadline to hold the seat.

question: What is a class number?
answer: The class number is a 4- or 5-digit number that identifies when and where a specific class is held.
text: Registering for Classes: What is a class number? A 4- or 5-digit number identifying when and where a class is held.

question: Will I be able to register for classes if I owe money to the College?
answer: No. You must pay any outstanding balance at least 24 hours before you register.
text: Registering for Classes: Can I register if I owe money to the College? No. Pay any outstanding balance at least 24 hours before you register.

question: Do I have to see an advisor in order to register for classes?
answer: Meeting with an academic advisor before registering is always a good idea to stay on track for graduation. Advisement is at your campus Advisement and Career Services office. First-time-in-college students coming directly from high school (direct entry) must attend mandatory orientation and meet with an advisor before registering. Continuing or returning students in good academic standing may see an advisor optionally, but it is strongly recommended. Students on academic probation must meet with an advisor each semester before registering.
text: Registering for Classes: Do I have to see an advisor to register? Direct-entry students must attend orientation and see an advisor first. Continuing students in good standing may see one optionally, though it is recommended. Students on academic probation must meet with an advisor each semester.

question: Can I take courses at any MDC campus, center, or off-campus location?
answer: Yes. As an MDC student you may take classes at any College location; there is no need to transfer between campuses because MDC is one college. Choosing a campus closest to home is a preference, not a requirement. Some programs and courses are offered only at specific campuses. For example, aviation core courses are offered at Homestead Campus and airport locations, funeral services courses at North Campus, and dental hygiene at Medical Campus.
text: Registering for Classes: Can I take courses at any MDC campus, center, or off-campus location? Yes. MDC is one college, so you can take classes at any location. Some programs are offered only at specific campuses, such as aviation, funeral services, and dental hygiene.

question: Where can I find my registration appointment?
answer: Log in to your MDConnect Student Center. Your enrollment appointment displays in the Enrollment Dates box on the right side of the page. If enrollment is open for multiple terms, click Open Enrollment Dates or Details for more information. The priority registration calendar is also available.
text: Registering for Classes: Where can I find my registration appointment? In MDConnect Student Center, in the Enrollment Dates box on the right side of the page.

question: How do I view my degree audit (academic requirements report)?
answer: Log in to your MDConnect Student Center. In the Academics section, open the other academic drop-down and select Academic Requirements. The report that appears is your degree audit. If you see The Academic Requirements page is not available, it may be because you have never had an advisor run a report for you (an advisor must run one at least once), you have no primary degree-seeking program declared, or you recently changed majors (an advisor must run a new report). Visit the Advisement office in these cases.
text: Registering for Classes: How do I view my degree audit? In MDConnect Student Center, under Academics, select Academic Requirements. If it is unavailable, an advisor must run it first, or you may need to declare a degree-seeking program or re-run it after a major change.

question: How do I apply for graduation?
answer: For an Associate in Arts degree, visit your campus Advisement & Career Services office so an advisor can review your record and confirm eligibility. For an Associate in Science, a College Credit Certificate, or a Bachelor's degree, contact the academic department that houses your pathway or major and meet with a program advisor. In both cases you must fill out an Application for Graduation form.
text: Graduation: How do I apply for graduation? Fill out an Application for Graduation form. AA students see their campus Advisement & Career Services office; AS, certificate, and bachelor's students see their academic department's program advisor.

question: When is graduation or commencement?
answer: You are certified for graduation at the end of your last semester. To be certified and receive your diploma, you must submit the graduation application by the deadline on the academic calendar. Commencement is held once a year at the end of the spring semester (late April or early May). Campus ceremony dates and times are posted on the College's Commencement page, updated annually.
text: Graduation: When is graduation or commencement? Commencement is once a year at the end of spring semester (late April or early May). You must submit your graduation application by the academic calendar deadline.

question: When will I receive my diploma?
answer: Diplomas are not handed out at the commencement ceremony. They are printed and mailed by the Admissions Office after all program requirements are met, usually about six to eight weeks after coursework is completed, to the address on record with Admissions. If your diploma seems delayed, or you are an MDC graduate needing a replacement, contact the Admissions Office.
text: Graduation: When will I receive my diploma? It is mailed by the Admissions Office about six to eight weeks after coursework is complete, not handed out at commencement.

question: I lost my diploma. How do I get a new one?
answer: Fill out the diploma reorder form and submit it with payment to the Admissions & Registration office.
text: Graduation: I lost my diploma. How do I get a new one? Submit the diploma reorder form with payment to the Admissions & Registration office.

question: The name on my diploma is misspelled. What do I do?
answer: If the name on your diploma is misspelled, contact your campus Admissions & Registration office to request a new one.
text: Graduation: The name on my diploma is misspelled. What do I do? Contact your campus Admissions & Registration office to request a new diploma.

question: Why doesn't my diploma have my major on it?
answer: This is not a mistake. Associate in Arts diplomas do not state the major.
text: Graduation: Why doesn't my diploma have my major on it? Associate in Arts diplomas do not list the major. This is not an error.

question: Where and when do I get my cap and gown for the ceremony? Is there a fee?
answer: If you have applied for graduation, pick up your cap and gown at your campus bookstore with your Student ID. There is no cost. Pick-up dates are posted on the Commencement page, usually closer to the ceremony.
text: Graduation: Where and when do I get my cap and gown? Pick them up free of charge at your campus bookstore with your Student ID, after applying for graduation. Dates are on the Commencement page.

question: What is a MAP?
answer: A MAP (My Academic Plan) is an individualized education plan that forecasts the path to graduation, laying out semester-by-semester the courses needed for a chosen degree. To view a MAP, log in to the web version of MDC Navigate and click planner. To develop, review, or update a MAP, meet with an academic advisor; see the Advisement and Career Services website to schedule. A MAP is also required for a Financial Aid Academic Appeal, and you must follow it and make academic progress to receive future aid. Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) rules apply to all federal aid recipients. Contact Financial Aid for details.
text: Advisement: What is a MAP? A My Academic Plan is a semester-by-semester course plan toward graduation, built with an advisor. View it in the web version of MDC Navigate under planner. It is also required for a financial aid academic appeal.

question: How do I calculate my grade point average?
answer: Multiply the number of units in each course by the point value of the letter grade you earned to get total grade points. Then divide total grade points by total credit hours attempted.
text: Advisement: How do I calculate my grade point average? Multiply each course's units by its grade point value, then divide total grade points by total credit hours attempted.

question: Can I repeat a course that I have not passed?
answer: You may repeat a course taken at MDC if you received a W, U, D, or F. Two attempts are allowed for a single course. A third or fourth attempt is granted at the department's discretion, and an out-of-state surcharge applies if approved. All attempts appear on the transcript, and GPA is recalculated using the final attempt only. To request a third or fourth attempt, contact the academic department responsible for the course. You may need a SMART plan with academic affairs (see www.mdc.edu/smart/). A W is not permitted on a third or fourth attempt.
text: Advisement: Can I repeat a course that I have not passed? Yes, if you received a W, U, D, or F. Two attempts are allowed; a third or fourth needs department approval and carries an out-of-state surcharge. GPA uses the final attempt only.

question: How many units can I take during the summer?
answer: The summer term has a first six-week session, a second six-week session, and a twelve-week session (see the academic calendar). Students in clear academic standing may take a maximum of 12 units for the full summer term and no more than 6 units in any six-week session. For example, 6 units in each six-week session is allowed; 9 units in the first and 3 in the second is not. Students on academic probation are limited to 6 units for the whole summer and should see an advisor before registering.
text: Advisement: How many units can I take during the summer? Up to 12 units for the full summer term, with no more than 6 units per six-week session. Students on academic probation are limited to 6 units.

question: What does it mean when my grade is W?
answer: A W means withdrawal after the last day to withdraw without penalty. No refund is issued. A W is not included in GPA, but too many W's can affect academic standing. Standards of Academic Progress require earning at least 67 percent of registered credits. Dropping a class after the 100-percent refund date counts as an attempt, and attempting more credits than you earn can lead to academic probation or suspension. W's are permanent on the transcript. Classes dropped after the 100-percent refund date still appear on your schedule. There is a deadline for dropping a class with a W, listed on your schedule or the academic calendar.
text: Advisement: What does it mean when my grade is W? A W is a withdrawal after the penalty-free drop deadline. It is not in GPA, no refund is issued, and it is permanent. Students must earn at least 67 percent of registered credits to stay in good standing.
